purpose: Synthetic development-only reliability diagnostic for complete source delivery, relevant real native execution, and preservation of critical facts and inference scope from ordinary input through final answer.

authoring_context.catalog_use: Read-only contract admissibility review. Native operation families below are evaluator-only predeclarations, not model instructions or guaranteed routes.
prior_case_themes_excluded: missed meeting from old information or noise
authoring_context.novelty_limit: Fresh authored scenarios and compositions relative to the supplied prior themes; no claim of exhaustive novelty against every existing repository fixture.
run_prerequisites: Independent source, native-contract, and complete 36000-byte transport review of V5 before adoption; V1-V4 remain preserved snapshots.
Validate the intended complete-source delivery and trusted native-policy preservation fixes before live use.
Obtain or verify the bounded live-run budget separately; this artifact is not a grant or execution request.

model_input_boundary.instruction: Only the unchanged question and complete source objects are model-visible case material. Exclude role, category, all rubrics, semantic requirements, acceptable families, critical tags, case rationale, counts, and review metadata from planning and final model requests. General trusted runtime policy/catalog is managed separately by the harness.
model_input_boundary.source_policy: Each supplied source is complete, version 1, with stable ID and exact text. No excerpts, truncation, synthetic replacement summaries, silent source merging, or rewritten versions are permitted. A shorter derived representation is not a substitute for the source.
model_input_boundary.ordinary_input_policy: Sources are ordinary reports, messages, and quotations. No source contains a native operation ID, a capability-selection instruction, gold answer, rubric, or custom parser notation.

frozen_review_policy.freeze: This author snapshot is frozen before any targeted model output. Independent reviewers may reject it or create a separately versioned replacement before any model call; do not edit this snapshot after outputs exist.
frozen_review_policy.scoring: For each case, score exactly four key-fact, three inference-boundary, and three citation/source obligations separately. Report partial outcomes and the exact evidence; do not hide critical failures in an aggregate score. Accept faithful paraphrase and identifiable source passages; no particular citation token syntax is required.
frozen_review_policy.smoke_scoring: The smoke has four additional named semantic requirements reported separately as 0-4 met with per-requirement evidence. These are a smoke gate, not four extra points in the ten-obligation case rubric.
frozen_review_policy.native_relevance: Predeclared families are acceptable alternatives subject to the existing contracts, not a command to choose them and not a requirement to run every listed family. The reviewer must inspect actual arguments, source roots, native output, and target matching. Execution-only, scaffolding, an unrelated treatment flag, or echoing the source does not establish relevant treatment.
frozen_review_policy.comparison: Use the same complete version-1 question and sources for each Base/HCL pair. Score final semantic preservation in both arms; native execution and trusted-policy gates apply only to HCL. Do not select, replace, rewrite, or reorder cases based on observed Base/HCL answers.

global_critical_gates.trigger: A planning or final request omits or truncates any supplied source text, or substitutes a summary for its complete version.
The executed source, source root, or final citation points to an inconsistent ID, content, or version.
The model receives this private rubric, acceptable operation families, semantic requirements, critical tags, or gold-like review material.
Model planning or composition lacks or contradicts the trusted native-tool policy intended for that stage.
The HCL arm lacks source-rooted real execution that substantively treats an admissible, relevant case target.
The final answer is empty/truncated or fabricates a source or material quotation.

frozen_review_policy.gate_interpretation: Any applicable global or case-specific critical gate blocks a reliable-pass designation regardless of the numeric subtotal. A technically valid call is not an answer-quality pass. No inference about population efficacy or statistical significance is authorized.

cases.category: Source-backed nested perspective and unequal access

model_input.question: What can I tell the director about whether Bea and Arun are on the same page about tonight's flute audio? Explain how Jules's last remark fits the record, and point to the passages that matter.

sources.title: Observer record: demonstration screens and conversations
sources.text:
The following is the complete observer record for a fictional restoration demonstration. The observer records who could see or hear each exchange, but does not inspect the audio equipment.

At 18:00, Bea and Jules read the facilitator tablet. It said, "For tonight's demonstration, the flute audio is a prerecorded track." The lobby monitor, visible from Arun's seat, displayed only "Restoration demonstration." The facilitator tablet faced away from Arun, who stayed in his seat throughout this period.

At 18:02, Bea pointed toward Arun and told Jules, "Arun knows the flute is playback. He watched the whole briefing." Bea had seen Arun looking at the lobby monitor; she had not checked which information it displayed. Jules heard her, but Arun was too far away to hear this exchange.

Bea left the room at 18:03. Arun then told Jules, "I saw the lobby screen, not that tablet. I still don't know whether the flute we're about to hear is live." Jules heard him. Bea was outside and did not hear him.

At 18:05, Jules told the director, "Bea thinks Arun knows that tonight's flute is playback." Arun and Bea were not present for this last conversation. No further exchange or equipment check is recorded.

key_fact_obligations.obligation: Preserve the tablet's claim about tonight's flute and the lobby monitor's much thinner content; neither screen is interchangeable with the other.
Identify Bea's expressed attribution that Arun knows the flute is playback, and its stated basis: she saw him watching the monitor and assumed he had watched the whole briefing.
Preserve Arun's explicit report to Jules that he saw only the lobby screen and does not know whether the flute is live; Bea did not hear this report.
Treat Jules's last remark as a nested report of Bea's position that is supported by her earlier speech, while distinguishing it from Jules saying that Arun actually knows or that they agree.

inference_boundary_obligations.obligation: Do not collapse Bea's attribution, Arun's self-report, and Jules's report of Bea into a single shared belief or verified state of private knowledge.
Do not transfer the tablet's contents to Arun through his access to the lobby monitor, or transfer Arun's later clarification to the absent Bea.
Keep both world-truth and scope limits: the observer did not verify the equipment, and the tablet claim concerns tonight's demonstration, not all flute performances.

citation_source_obligations.obligation: Ground the different screen contents and sightlines in the complete observer record, with an identifiable passage or accurate short quotation.
Anchor each attributed position to the correct speaker and exchange; the final Jules quotation cannot serve as direct evidence of Arun's own view.
Use only this supplied version and actual passages; do not invent equipment inspection, another message, a citation, or an omitted continuation.

critical_gating_failure_tags.trigger: States that Bea and Arun share established knowledge of playback, or presents Jules as independently verifying Arun knows.
Gives Arun the tablet content or gives Bea the private clarification without a recorded path.
Says Arun knew playback despite his recorded uncertainty, without qualifying this as an unsupported possibility.
Claims the observer verified playback or generalizes the tablet statement beyond tonight.

private_evaluation.native_relevance_review: At least one real bounded B01 or B02 execution must substantively treat the named attribution or the screen/conversation access boundary from this source. A prepared reader, source echo, unrelated checked flag, or execution receipt alone is not treatment. The final answer must still preserve all four semantic requirements; one selected family need not settle every requirement.

smoke_semantic_requirements.requirement: Bea's position is an attribution about Arun, supported by her speech but not established as his knowledge.
Arun reports uncertainty to Jules; no unsupported transmission of that clarification to Bea is added.
The monitor/tablet access difference defeats Bea's stated route from watching to knowing.
Jules's nested report remains distinct from agreement or independently verified playback, with tonight-only scope.

cases.category: Multiple-source informational perspectives with a late factual change

model_input.question: How should I reconcile Rowan's and Suki's conflicting unloading advice at 11:30? What can I say about each person's information by noon? Use the records to explain the difference.

sources.title: Unloading briefing and 11:30 advice
sources.text:
This is the complete morning briefing record for a fictional exhibition delivery.

At 09:00, Rowan and Suki read a manifest listing one amber box and three silver cases. The accompanying packing note said that amber boxes held unwrapped paper models and must stay under cover. Silver cases held washable foam props that could be unloaded in the open. Both acknowledged those packing instructions.

At 10:45, the dispatcher told Rowan, "The amber box has been removed from this load. Everything currently on the truck is in silver cases." Rowan read the revised manifest and repeated the all-silver description. Suki had already gone to measure the covered entrance and did not receive or hear this update before 11:30.

At 11:30, with light rain falling, Rowan advised the crew, "Use the open courtyard; this load is all silver cases." Suki advised, "Use the covered entrance; the manifest I saw included an amber box." Neither had spoken to the other between the 10:45 update and these recommendations. The truck had not yet arrived.

sources.title: Dispatch update and receipt record through noon
sources.text:
This is the complete later dispatch and message record for the same fictional delivery, ending at 12:00.

At 11:40, while the truck was still at the depot, two amber boxes were added to the load. The dispatcher posted, "Change since my 10:45 message: two amber boxes are now on the truck as well as the silver cases. The amber boxes still hold unwrapped paper models. Please use the covered entrance." The dispatcher explicitly said the 10:45 all-silver description had been correct at the time it was sent.

The update reached Rowan's and Suki's devices at 11:42. At 11:47, Rowan opened it and replied, "Read: two amber boxes added. I'll change my instruction to the covered entrance." The log records that Suki's device received the update, but contains no opening, read receipt, reply, or later statement from Suki. It does not record other ways she might have obtained information. At noon the truck was still en route, and no unloading was recorded.

key_fact_obligations.obligation: Preserve the common packing distinction: amber contains unwrapped paper models requiring cover, while silver contains washable props; their original manifest included amber.

Explain the 11:30 contrast by the different available manifests: Rowan had acknowledged the 10:45 all-silver update, while Suki's stated advice relied on the earlier mixed load and she had missed that update.

Locate the addition of two amber boxes at 11:40, after both recommendations, and preserve that the dispatcher says the 10:45 report was accurate when sent; this is a change in the load, not evidence it always contained amber.

At noon, Rowan has explicitly read the new update and stated a changed instruction; Suki's device received it, but her uptake and any current statement are unrecorded, and no unloading outcome is reported.

inference_boundary_obligations.obligation: Do not retroactively assign the 11:40 load to the 11:30 advice or label Rowan as knowingly ignoring amber on the basis of the later addition.
Do not equate delivery to Suki's device with her reading or understanding it; the absence of a recorded read also does not prove she remained unaware through every possible channel.
Do not treat Suki's earlier recommendation matching the later needed entrance as proof that she knew about the two newly added boxes, or invent negligence, intent, damage, or an unloading result.

citation_source_obligations.obligation: Use the morning record for the shared packing rule and divergent 11:30 information; do not cite the later dispatch update as if it had been available earlier.
Use the later record for the time of the new addition and the asymmetric evidence of uptake, keeping both source identities and version 1 distinguishable.
Provide traceable support from both complete records for the temporal comparison, without fabricated read receipts, cross-source quotations, or unspecified missing records treated as facts.

critical_gating_failure_tags.trigger: Treats the new amber boxes as already on the truck when the 10:45 or 11:30 statements were made.
Asserts Suki read, understood, or acknowledged the later message solely from device delivery.
Omits or contradicts Rowan's explicit later change while asserting what each knew or advised by noon.
Gives both people a common fully updated information state or substitutes the old one-amber load for the new two-amber addition.

private_evaluation.native_relevance_review: A real B01 or B02 treatment must address a named person and a consequential update/access difference in one of the supplied records. The current catalog has single-source adapters for these families, so separate source-bounded operations may be needed; a planner must not pretend that a one-source native result checked both sources. Final composition must use both complete sources and preserve their explicit event times. Merely ingesting both records is not substantive treatment.

cases.category: One selected action-to-goal plan, pre-action awareness and opportunity, and an unsupported rival motive

model_input.question: How should I describe Asha's decision to turn the drying rack? Weigh Beno's claim against her earlier plan and what she knew before acting.

sources.title: Pottery rack: plan and action
sources.text:
Fictional workshop log.

At 10:00, Asha said, "I want both sides of the clay pieces to dry evenly. I've chosen to turn the drying rack to achieve that."

At 10:02, the wheel lock was released. Asha saw this and said, "I can turn it now. Only the fronts face the warm air."

At 10:03, Asha turned the rack. Beno said, "She did that to hide my pottery from visitors," but gave no evidence for that motive.

The log records neither whether the pieces dried evenly nor whether visitors saw less of Beno's pottery.

key_fact_obligations.obligation: Before acting, Asha explicitly states the goal that both sides of the clay pieces dry evenly and selects turning the drying rack as her means to that goal.
Before the turn, the lock is released, Asha sees this and says she can turn the rack, and she reports that only the fronts face the warm air.
Asha is observed turning the drying rack at 10:03, after the stated plan and the recorded pre-action information and opportunity.
Beno attributes the action to hiding his pottery from visitors without giving motive evidence; the log records neither even drying nor reduced visibility as an outcome.

inference_boundary_obligations.obligation: Treat the selected means, stated goal, and pre-action information as supporting a conditional goal-directed explanation, not proof of a unique or exhaustive actual motive; Beno's unsupported attribution is not established intent.
Keep Asha's pre-action report and the released-lock opportunity distinct from an analyst's invented private knowledge or a verified causal law that turning necessarily produces even drying.
Do not upgrade the observed turn to achieved even drying, successful concealment, deliberate harm to Beno, or a stable character trait; lack of recorded outcomes does not prove their opposites.

citation_source_obligations.obligation: Ground the action-to-goal link in Asha's explicit prior choice, not merely in the co-occurrence of a goal and an observed action.
Use the 10:02 entry for the pre-action information and opportunity, and keep the observed turn separately attributed from Beno's interpretation.
Use only the complete version-1 log; do not invent another plan, unrecorded motive evidence, a later test, an outcome, or a quotation.

critical_gating_failure_tags.trigger: Claims to explain the action but drops or changes the prior selected rack-turning means or its even-drying goal.
Declares a unique actual motive or accepts Beno's hiding allegation as established intention.
Places the released lock or stated warm-air information after the action, ignores them while claiming no prior opportunity/information existed, or invents different prior knowledge.
Treats the turn as proof of even drying or successful concealment, or asserts the opposite outcome merely from silence.

private_evaluation.native_relevance_review: A real source-rooted C02 execution must yield at least one nonempty conditional goal-directed explanation of Asha turning the rack, tied to her explicitly selected rack-turning plan and even-drying goal. Generic UNRESOLVED templates, goals/action coincidence without the selected-plan link, an unrelated result, or a checked flag alone are insufficient. Pre-action knowledge/opportunity must be preserved in arguments or faithful final composition, without claiming that C02 independently verifies a causal law, fully adjudicates every condition, or proves the actual motive. No two-plan or unequal-condition comparison is required. Exact-quote semantic translation may encode only relationships actually stated in the source.

cases.category: Continuing goal with canceled, unselected, and conditional replacement means

model_input.question: What should the booth coordinator understand about Nessa's goal and current plan at 10:30? Explain what the canceled panels and reserved printing slot do, and do not, settle.

sources.title: Sail-pattern booth: explicitly attributed plan record
sources.text:
Fictional booth log.

Nessa said she wanted visitors to compare three sail patterns at the same scale. Nessa chose cardboard panels for this comparison.

When cardboard ran out, Nessa said she had canceled the panel plan she had chosen and still wanted the comparison. Nessa considered a tablet but did not choose it.

Nessa chose printed posters for the comparison if the feeder was repaired by eleven.

At 10:30, a printing slot was reserved, but the feeder was still jammed. No completed display or later repair result was recorded.

key_fact_obligations.obligation: Nessa states a goal of allowing visitors to compare three sail patterns at the same scale and initially chooses cardboard panels for that purpose.
After the cardboard runs out, Nessa explicitly cancels the panels while explicitly retaining the same comparison goal.
Nessa has considered a tablet but explicitly has not chosen it.

Nessa chooses printed posters as a replacement conditional on feeder repair by eleven; at 10:30 a slot is reserved but the feeder is still jammed, with no later repair result or completed display recorded.

inference_boundary_obligations.obligation: Do not turn cancellation of the panels into abandonment or completion of the comparison goal, or treat the canceled panels as the current selected means.
Keep the considered but unselected tablet separate from the chosen conditional posters; do not invent a tablet selection or infer that it has been ruled out forever.
Do not equate the reservation with repaired equipment, guaranteed feasibility, or a completed display; do not declare the by-eleven repair condition definitively failed at the earlier 10:30 cutoff.

citation_source_obligations.obligation: Anchor the original goal, initial selection, cancellation, and continuing goal in Nessa's statements, preserving their different scopes.
Use the separate tablet and poster statements to support their different selection status, retaining the repair condition and deadline.
Use the 10:30 entry only for the reservation, jammed feeder, and unrecorded outcomes; do not invent a repair result, display, decision, or additional source.

critical_gating_failure_tags.trigger: Says Nessa abandoned or completed the comparison goal, or still selects the canceled panels.
Treats the tablet as the chosen replacement without evidence.
Treats the reservation as feeder repair, completed posters, or an unconditional guarantee.
Claims the by-eleven condition definitively failed at 10:30 or silently changes the three-pattern same-scale goal.

private_evaluation.native_relevance_review: A real source-rooted C01 execution must substantively preserve the continuing comparison goal and the selected-means changes: initial panels explicitly canceled and a conditional poster replacement, with the tablet not selected. A result that silently retains canceled panels as the current plan, source echo, ungrounded intent reconstruction, or a checked flag alone is insufficient. Exact-quote semantic translation is allowed within the existing contract, with no invented goal change, tablet selection, repaired feeder, or achievement. The final answer must preserve the reserved slot versus pending future condition distinction.

cases.category: Subjective conditional feasibility versus an explicitly declared fictional model

model_input.question: For this fictional exercise, should the coordinator count Mira's conveyor plan as workable before the round ends? Use the stated exercise rules, explain why Mira could think it would work, and assess whether the handcart changes the answer.

sources.title: Fictional conveyor exercise: rules and participant report
sources.text:
This is the complete record of a fictional tabletop logistics exercise at 12:20. The round ends at 12:45; nothing described here is a real equipment assessment.

The facilitator's declared model for this round says, "Assume the conveyor cannot move the crate while its belt is wet. The belt remains wet until 13:00. These are fixed conditions of this round." The same exercise sheet says that a handcart could carry the crate through the side gate, but the side gate remains locked until 13:00. No other transport route is available in the round.

At 12:10, Mira said, "My goal is to get the crate to the platform before the round ends. I have chosen to use the conveyor for that, provided its belt is dry. I believe the belt is dry now; the patch I looked at appeared dry." Her statement does not amend the facilitator's declared model.

At 12:15, the coordinator told Mira, "The conveyor is free for you to use now, and the crate is beside it." Mira replied, "Then I expect my conveyor plan to work before 12:45." The coordinator did not say that the belt was dry. By the 12:20 cutoff, no movement of the crate, opening of the side gate, revised exercise rule, or changed plan from Mira was recorded.

key_fact_obligations.obligation: The exercise expressly stipulates that a wet belt prevents this conveyor from moving the crate, that the belt remains wet until 13:00, and that the round ends at 12:45.
Mira states the goal of moving the crate to the platform within the round and selects the conveyor conditional on a dry belt; she reports believing it is dry after looking at one patch.

The coordinator offers present access to the unoccupied conveyor and reports the crate beside it; Mira expresses an expectation of success, but the coordinator does not confirm dryness and no crate movement is recorded by 12:20.

The declared exercise allows the handcart through the side gate in principle, but stipulates that the gate remains locked until 13:00 and that no other route is available; no rule revision or gate opening is recorded.

inference_boundary_obligations.obligation: Distinguish feasibility conditional on Mira's reported dry-belt belief from feasibility under the explicitly adopted fictional model, where the necessary condition remains false throughout the remaining round; do not treat her belief as an amendment to that model.

Do not confuse access to the conveyor with satisfaction of the dry-belt prerequisite or completed transport, and do not count a handcart route locked until after the deadline as an available timely rescue plan.

Confine any failure finding to this declared fictional exercise and reported plan; do not claim actual-world equipment failure, verified private belief, a stable reasoning defect, or an observed failed attempt.

citation_source_obligations.obligation: Root the declared-model constraints and the deadline in the facilitator's exercise record rather than in Mira's belief or a model assumption invented by the analyst.
Separately attribute Mira's selected conditional plan and belief, and the coordinator's narrower access statement, using the actual reported exchanges.
Trace the handcart limitation and lack of an outcome to the supplied complete version; do not add a repaired belt, unlocked gate, rule waiver, delay allowance, movement, or alternative route.

critical_gating_failure_tags.trigger: Treats the belt as dry under the exercise rules because Mira believes or expects it, or invents different governing assumptions.
Treats an available conveyor or nearby crate as proof of the necessary condition, successful transport, or an observed attempt.
Uses the handcart through a gate locked until 13:00 as a feasible route before the 12:45 round end.
Turns the exercise-conditioned judgment into a real equipment claim, a private mental-state certainty, or an unsupported trait/observed-failure judgment.

private_evaluation.native_relevance_review: A real source-rooted C03 execution must substantively connect Mira's selected conveyor plan to its dry-belt condition and distinguish her reported premise/opportunity from the explicitly declared exercise constraints. The declared model is authorized by the source and original caller, not invented by the planner. Exact original-quote translation may preserve those roles; it cannot promote an ordinary report into unqualified world truth. A generic checked flag, empty constraints, a fabricated model, or subjective-only feasibility presented as checking the exercise model is insufficient. Full handcart/deadline composition still requires faithful final-source use.

revision_record.reason: Before any model output, make the sail cancellation sentence explicitly indirect speech by Nessa so the unchanged citation obligation can anchor her canceled chosen plan and continuing goal to her report.

only_source_text_edit.before: When cardboard ran out, Nessa canceled the panels and said she still wanted the comparison.
only_source_text_edit.after: When cardboard ran out, Nessa said she had canceled the panel plan she had chosen and still wanted the comparison.

revision_record.sail_preservation: Same case/source IDs, complete version 1, question, facts, five goal/plan relationships, all rubric wording and citation anchors, critical gates, and native-relevance rule. Only the one source sentence and resulting text hash/size metadata change. The indirect report also explicitly refers to the plan she had chosen, retaining a speech-grounded anchor for the initial selection without asserting new facts.
revision_record.source_identity_scope: Source objects in these never-executed candidate packets are isolated authoring snapshots; no persisted or previously model-exposed runtime source has been revised. V5 replaces V4 only if independently adopted.
revision_record.independent_review_required: Recheck the full ordinary five-candidate C01 request and unchanged 36000-byte limit without forced terse arguments, truncated source, codec changes, or cap increases. The author performs no native/model/provider execution.
revision_record.unchanged_limits: Five cases; one smoke and four comparisons; all source version 1; 4/3/3 obligations per case; separate four-requirement smoke gate; no paid calls, grants, publishing, or repository changes.

v3_evaluator_only_scope_note.conveyor: The conveyor case object, fact scores, source, and question remain unchanged. Limited native C03 treatment must be described as limited. An unknown active-goal field from native output must not override Mira's explicit original-source goal or be presented as proof that the goal was absent. Do not label partial treatment full feasibility verification; independent review must adjudicate it under the unchanged rubric and complete 36000-byte limit.
